courses.title: 第 01 集｜46 Linden Street｜Act 1
courses.description: 理查德在史泰登岛渡轮上拍照，遇到交换生亚历山德拉，并展示《走遍美国》照片集。

sentences.content: In act one, he takes pictures of New York City on the Staten Island Ferry.
He shows Alexandra some pictures for Family Album USA.
It's an album of pictures of the United States.
Hi, my name is Richard Stewart.
May I take a picture of you and your little boy?
Well, it's a book of pictures.
I call it Family Album USA.
Well, it's fine if you take our picture.
Now give mommy a kiss, Gerald.
We'll be looking for your book.
Here, let me take your picture.
it's not finished yet, but I have some of the pictures.
Would you like to see them?
It's an album of pictures of the United States, the cities, the special places, and the people,
and these are pictures of people working.
There are steelworkers, bankers, police, street vendors, and ambulance drivers.
Oh, and this is my father.
My younger brother, Robbie, he goes to high school.
She works for a toy company.
And this is my wife, Marilyn.
That's a large city in northern Greece, but now I'm living in the Bronx.
I have to meet my wife.
it was a pleasure meeting you, too.
Thanks for your help, and good luck.
It's an album of pictures of the United States.
Richard takes many pictures for his album.
He photographs the cities, like New York.
Philip Stewart, Richard's father, is a doctor.
He's a pediatrician, a children's doctor.
And Richard's mother, Ellen Stewart, is a homemaker.
His brother, Robbie, is a student at Riverdale High School.
She works for a toy company in New York City.
He's 72 years old and lives in Florida.
And this is Richard's wife, Marilyn Stewart.
She's a fashion designer and a sales clerk in a boutique in New York City.
You'll meet Marilyn Stewart and all the other Stewarts in Family Album USA.

courses.description: 斯图尔特一家共进晚餐，理查德因丢失相机包而烦恼，门铃响起，有人来访。

sentences.content: In Act Three, the Stewart family has dinner together.
Richard is upset about losing his camera bag.
I keep thinking about that bag of film.
And his mother, Ellen, tries to help.
Don't worry, Richard, someone will find it.
And give her a teaspoon of the medicine after every meal.
They'll be here soon, and then we'll eat.
She has to work late tonight.
And what's Robbie cooking for dinner?
Don't worry, we've got lots of ice cream.
Oh, I'd love some ice cream.
Well, there's chocolate, coffee, and a little vanilla.
I'll have vanilla, is that all right with everyone?
One scoop of coffee and one scoop of chocolate for me.
Robbie, will you help me serve?
I keep thinking about that bag of film.
Eight rolls, a whole day's work, and good stuff, too.
Your brother left his bag of film on the ferry boat.
Gee, I'm really glad to see you.
I mean, my brother'll be really glad to see you.
Oh, yes, Richard told us all about you.
And this is my mother, Ellen Stewart.
And my father, Dr. Philip Stewart.
I'm so glad you found the bag and took the time and trouble to return it.
I just took the wrong train.
Would you like something to eat?
I'm late for dinner at my house.
Would you like to call home?
Alexandra's a high school exchange student from Greece.
With a family in the Bronx.
Oh, that's not too far from here.
I can only stay a few minutes.
Where do you go to school?
At the Bronx High School of Science.
Oh, that's a very good school.
Richard tells me you're a doctor.
And what does your father do?
It might be a little cold.
It was nice meeting you all.
Well, maybe you'll come for lunch some Sunday so we can really thank you for bringing Richard's bag back.
The train is just up the street.
It won't take me long at all.
Well, you really saved the day for me, Alexandra.
She's a smart young lady, and very nice.
Oh, I guess we'll be seeing Alexandra again.
Oh, yes, Richard told us all about you.
And this is my mother, Ellen Stewart.
And my father, Dr. Philip Stewart.
It was nice meeting you, Robbie.

courses.title: 第 08 集｜Grandpa's Trunk｜Act 2
courses.description: 爷爷乘火车去纽约，遇到埃尔莎·托宾，聊天中透露家人希望他永久同住，但他犹豫。

sentences.content: In the second act, Grandpa travels to New York City on the train
And meets a woman named Elsa Tobin.
They enjoy talking to each other.
You said you have family in New York.
Grandpa is looking forward to seeing his family, but does he want to stay with them permanently?
Are you going to live with them?
Oh, let me help you with this.
Do you want to sit by the window?
I like the aisle seat better.
Please, you sit by the window.
My name is Stuart, Malcolm Stuart.
Do you, live in New York?
But, didn't you just get on?
A man next to me was smoking, and smoke really bothers me.
Where are you from in Florida?
My husband and I live near Spaceport.
My house is, only a few miles from Spaceport.
He couldn't take time off to come to New York with me.
I sold the house and the furniture,
Put a few personal things in an old trunk, and shipped it to my children in New York.
My wife died four years ago.
She was a wonderful woman, a real friend.
John and I celebrate our 40th anniversary next month.
He's an aerospace engineer and works for Orlando Aircraft Corporation.
He started with them almost 40 years ago.
Had my own company, a construction company.
But I just sold it and retired.
Would you kindly hold these keys, please?
I have a ticket, I know.
I was in the smoking section.
I'm sure it's in your purse, Mrs. Tobin.
Do you, have family in New York?
No, but I do have very close friends in New York City.
We like to go to the theater together.
You said you have family in New York.
A son and his wife and their three children, my grandchildren.
Oh, I can't wait to see them.
Are you going to live with them?
But it's too early to know for sure.
I tried to teach my kids the importance of independence,
But I'm not sure I want to be alone.
Some people don't mind being alone.
But tell me, why did you stop working?
I wanted to be with my family.
I didn't want to be alone anymore.
My name is Stuart, Malcolm Stuart.
Are you married, yes or no?
John and I celebrate our 40th anniversary next month.
Are you a doctor, a farmer, a mailman?
A lawyer, an artist, a salesman?
Do you have family in New York?
Do you have family in New York?

courses.title: 第 09 集｜Grandpa's Trunk｜Act 3
courses.description: 爷爷到达纽约，家人为他准备礼物。他打开行李箱，旧照片和回忆让一家人温馨团聚。

sentences.content: In the third act, Grandpa arrives in New York.
And the night is full of surprises.
Ladies and gentlemen, Amtrak is happy to announce our arrival in New York City.
The train will be stopping in five minutes.
Please check to be sure you have your belongings, and have a good stay in the Big Apple.
It was so nice meeting you, Mr. Stewart.
And nice meeting you, too, Mrs. Tobin.
And have a good time in New York.
You're very lucky to have a caring family.
And we'll take your dad with us.
Let's give him our presents, now.
I looked all over the house to find it.
This one really brings back memories.
She called to say the plane was delayed.
I can't wait to see her.
She looks just like Grandma at that age.
Don't you want something to eat?
I, after a good night's sleep I'll enjoy breakfast even more.
Ellen and I will take you to your room.
I'm sure glad you're here, Grandpa.
Do you have the key to the trunk?
I have the key, but it doesn't work.
I researched it for over a year.
I didn't know that your grandfather was born in Germany.
Lots of interesting information about our family.
I'm so happy to see you.
Oh, you look so beautiful, Susan.
Like I always said, you look just like Grandma.
I think you're going to be very happy here with us.
Malcolm Stewart is not alone anymore, that's for sure.
In fact, he'll have his family around him every day of his life now.
Finding some peace and quiet may be a little difficult.
But my father won't be lonely anymore.
He has me, Philip Stewart, nearby, and the rest of his family.
You know, I met Ellen when I was a student at the University of Michigan.
Our oldest son is a photographer.
And she's also a sister-in-law to Susan.
Susan reminds us of her grandmother,
She was kind, intelligent, and lovable, like Susan.
He loves his grandfather very much.
Well, that's our family, the Stewarts.
Well, that's our family, and I love them all.

courses.title: 第 17 集｜Thanksgiving｜Act 2
courses.description: 感恩节游行中，爷爷试图让罗比开心，但罗比心不在焉。菲利普期待橄榄球赛，电话铃声响起，可能是亚历山德拉打来的。

sentences.content: In Act Two, Grandpa tries to cheer up Robbie.
Oh, look at that float, Robbie.
He wants to watch the football game.
What time does the Michigan football game come on?
The Thanksgiving Day Parade is always such great fun.
Oh, look at that, it's that Superman balloon.
Just floating along high above Central Parkway.
Oh, and the bands and the music.
John Philip Sousa, I love his music.
♫ Oh, look at that float, Robbie.
But parades always make me feel like a kid.
Remember when you and your dad and I went to the Thanksgiving Day Parade?
You were four or five years old, I think.
Yes, he missed a phone call from Alexandra.
Yes, I know, but he'll get over it.
I look forward to seeing you, and Harry and Michelle.
It's my favorite part of the meal.
What about my famous apple pie?
Dad, your apple pie is my favorite dessert.
Philip, would you join me in the kitchen, please?
No, honey, you just relax with Grandpa.
I'll get you to help serve later.
Ellen reminds me so much of Grandma.
What time does the Michigan football game come on?
I'll be back to see the game.
Grandpa, when did Dad graduate from Michigan?
He graduated from medical school in 1960,
And from the University of Michigan in 1956.
Did you go to Michigan too, Grandpa?
I've gotta start thinking about college soon.
Grandpa loves the Thanksgiving Day Parade.
Philip likes to make apple pie.
And Robbie is fond of Alexandra.
What time does the Michigan football game come on?
And Robbie is crazy about Alexandra.
Why does he always have to slam the door?
And Robbie hates waiting for Alexandra to call.
But Robbie really likes his mom's turkey dressing.
It's my favorite part of the meal.
And you can guess his favorite friend is.

courses.title: 第 19 集｜Man's Best Friend｜Act 1
courses.description: 罗比发现亚历山德拉因思念希腊家人而难过。他们听到奇怪声音，发现一只走失的小狗，决定帮助它找主人。

sentences.content: In act one, Robbie notices that Alexandra is unhappy about something.
She misses her family in Greece.
You really miss your family, don't you?
A little later, they hear a strange sound.
Robbie, this new Walkman is absolutely wonderful.
Richard and Marilyn bought it for me for my birthday.
You are very lucky, Robbie, to have such a nice family.
Come on, you can tell me.
I received a letter from my parents this morning.
Did they write some bad news?
Well, then why are you so sad?
The Molinas treat me so nicely,
and I love being with your family so much,
but when I received the letter with photographs of my family,
I cried because I miss them all.
You really miss your family, don't you?
I know I must seem silly.
It's not like I have nobody.
I like the Molinas very much, and they're so kind to me.
Hey, why don't we go out for a cheeseburger and french fries?
And you can use my Walkman.
But if we go out, please,
Don't complain about your math teacher or your math homework.
I have to turn off the lights, or else my father will get really angry.
He says I never turn them out when I leave.
If they come home and they're on.
It sounded like a dog barking.
Sounded like a dog barking right here.
Her name's Gemma, and she belongs to Mr. and Mrs. Levinson.
Robbie, maybe you should call them and tell the Levinsons we have their cute little spaniel.
I've always wanted a springer spaniel.
The number you are calling, 555-8448, is no longer in service.
The number's no longer in service.
Alexandra and I are such good friends.
We listen to music together and go places together and talk about things.
Like today, Alexandra was so unhappy, and I didn't understand why at first.
I received a letter from my parents this morning.
Did they write some bad news?
Well, then why are you so sad?
Then I realized that Alexandra was lonely.
She was so lonely without her family.
You really miss your family, don't you?
I know I must seem silly.
It's not like I have nobody.
I like the Molinas very much, and they're so kind to me.
I had to cheer her up.
We always have such a good time when we go out together.
Hey, why don't we go out for a cheeseburger and french fries?
She wasn't the only one who missed her family.
Gemma looked so lonely, with such a sad face, and Alexandra understood.

sentences.content: In Act Three, Robbie finds out how to adopt a dog.
If you want to adopt an animal, first we need to know some references.
Both Robbie and Alexandra would like to have a pet.
To have a friend, a pal.
You know, man's best friend is his dog.
Later on, Linda has news for Robbie.
We have good news and bad news, Robbie.
Will Linda find the owners, or will Robbie adopt Gemma?
If you want to adopt an animal, first we need to know some references.
We need to talk to some people about you.
We wanna be sure that you're responsible and that you can take good care of an animal.
Then you have to fill out this form about your family background.
We need to know about your history with animals.
Have you ever owned an animal?
We had a cat when I was eight years old.
Do you have any animals now?
We also like to know your reasons for wanting an animal.
Just to hold it and cuddle with it.
Just to have as a pet.
To have a friend, a pal.
You know, man's best friend is his dog.
And one thing more: if you're under 21 years of age- That's me.
Then an adult must sign for you.
My parents will think it's a good idea.
If the real owners don't come to claim Gemma.
After 48 hours, but please call first.
Thanks for your information and for being so helpful.
Nice talking to both of you.
Maybe the real owners will come to claim her.
I see you're both animal lovers.
We'll call in a couple of days.
Goodbye, and thanks for bringing Gemma in.
I keep thinking about the dog, about Gemma alone in the animal shelter.
I know, but I promise you, Alexandra, the dog is just fine.
They're very kind to the animals.
I mean about her being alone.
Even if they are kind to Gemma, she's still alone without her family.
I'll have the chef salad, please.
I will have a cheeseburger, medium rare, with raw onion and french fries, please.
Ginger ale with lots of ice for me, thank you.
Aren't you surprised that the animal shelter is so careful about finding homes for the animals?
And a cheeseburger, medium rare, with onion and french fries, and a ginger ale with lots of ice.
Hey, I wanted you to hear my new sound system when the dog scratched on the front door.
Let's finish eating, and then we'll go back to my house.
I want you to hear my new tapes.
I've got some great new dance music.
This is Linda Aborn from the animal shelter.
It's Linda from the animal shelter.
We have good news and bad news, Robbie.
The good news is that the Levinsons have come by to pick up the dog.
The bad news is you won't be able to adopt the dog.
Come by one day and look at some of the other dogs.
I'm sure there's one for you.
Thanks, Robbie, and the Levinsons thank you for bringing their dog to us.
She said if I come by, she'll help me find another dog.
They come in every shape, every size, and every color.
Long hair and short hair, or no hair at all.
Some come with feathers, and some have fur, and some will even come when you call.
I'm talking about pets in the USA.
Some you can hold, some will walk by your side, and some you can ride every day.
Some will shake your hand, and when they get to know you, they seem to understand what you say.
I'm talking 'bout pets in the USA.
No matter what they look like, no matter what they are, we like to think of them as our friends.
and they can be such good company.
Some live underwater, some live in a cage, and some can just walk around your home.
They may have droopy eyes, they may have floppy ears, but they can keep you from feeling all alone.
I'm talking 'bout pets in the USA.

courses.title: 第 23 集｜You're Going to Be Fine｜Act 2
courses.description: 护士莫莉与孩子们玩猜词游戏，但卡尔拒绝参与。斯图尔特医生试图了解卡尔不愿住院的原因。

sentences.content: In the second act, the nurse, Molly Baker, plays a game with the children at the hospital.
The name of the game is Charades.
But Carl Herrera won't play the game.
Why don't you, want to play?
Because I don't wanna be here.
Carl is upset because he wants something else.
Do you know how to play charades?
Carl, you sure you've never played?
Betty, Tim, and Frank, we're going to play charades.
Frank, you can learn as we go, and Carl, you join in at any time.
You've got that part right, yes.
The first word sounds like no.
The first word is snow, fifth word, seven.
Snow White and the Seven Dwarves.
Betty, you had it, but you didn't say it.
Between now and tomorrow, you're all going to have your tonsils out, and you won't be able to speak for a while, so save your voices till then.
I sure am glad to see you, Dr. Stewart.
I didn't wanna play charades, so they're angry at me.
Why don't you, want to play?
Because I don't wanna be here.
I don't want my tonsils out.
My mother promised me a birthday party with a clown.
But you can have one when you go home, Carl.
Carl, you'll have your party when you go home.
But it won't be on my birthday.
And you promised me a surprise.
Why is this ball in my bowl?
Pot, pat, rock, black, mop, map.
Eat, it, seek, sick, leap, lip.
And the ball is in his bowl.

sentences.content: In the first act, Robbie is writing a story for the Riverdale High School newspaper.
I'm writing an article on the feelings about graduation.
Robbie will have to make some decisions.
What does he want to do after graduation?

Philip would like Robbie to go to the University of Michigan,
so he schedules an interview for Robbie with the dean of admissions.

courses.title: 第 27 集｜It's Up to You｜Act 3
courses.description: 罗比告诉朋友迈克想学新闻，并与父亲菲利普讨论自己的决定，菲利普支持他。

sentences.content: In the third act, Robbie's friend, Mike, tells Robbie about his interview.
I had a great interview with admissions at Columbia University.
And Robbie tells Mike that he'd like to study journalism.
I think I wanna study journalism, to be a reporter.
Later, Robbie talks to his father about his decision.
I was just waiting for you to get home so we could talk.
How will Philip feel about Robbie's decision?
I had an interview today, too.
I had a great interview with admissions at Columbia University.
Will you get into the school?
Well, they didn't say anything for sure, but I figure that with my grades and with my personality, I'll have no problem.
It's not easy, and this is an important decision we have to make.
How was your interview with Michigan?
My father would like me to go there.
He and my grandpa both went there.
You can follow in your father's footsteps.
I'd like to follow in my own footsteps, Mike.
Yeah, what do you wanna study?
I think I wanna study journalism, to be a reporter, a newspaperman.
You do a pretty good job on the Riverdale High School paper.
And I've been thinking about it a lot lately.
Have you discussed it with your parents?
I was just waiting for you to get home so we could talk.
Anything special you wanna talk about?
I know you and Mom have given up a lot to save money for my college tuition.
We want you to go to college, Robbie.
Well, I thought a lot about which college,
And one of them is Columbia.
Well, first, they have an excellent school of journalism.
And your friends are planning to go to Columbia?
Mike and I had a hamburger this afternoon, and we talked.
Well, we talked about a lot of things.
He applied to Columbia, and his interview was very successful.
He thinks he'll be accepted, and he really wants to go there.
He told me he was very impressed with you.
You had some doubts about wanting to go to Michigan.
I'm just not sure about what I wanna do.
Let me tell you something, Robbie,
Well, Grandpa wanted me to study engineering, like him.
Well, I wasn't clear about my future, but
I knew engineering was not for me.
Then you're not upset about my not wanting to go into medicine?
I'm just happy that we're able to talk about it.
I suppose you want to apply to Columbia.
Yes, but I also wanna apply to several other colleges.
I thought you wanted to go to Columbia.
Well, I might wanna go to Columbia, and I might not.
I just wanna be able to make my own decision.
And if I think about it long enough, you never know.
If I make my own decision,
When I was your age, I said exactly the same thing to Grandpa.
Do I wanna go to the University of Michigan?
Or to an Ivy League school, like Columbia University.
Or maybe NYU, New York University.
I've also been thinking about going to a state school, SUNY, the State University of New York at New Paltz.
I think I'd like to go to a small school, but Michigan in Ann Arbor, Michigan, is not small.
SUNY at New Paltz is smaller than either Michigan or NYU, and Columbia is smaller than SUNY.
It's the smallest school for undergraduates.
I want to go to a school that's close to Riverdale.
Wow, that's a lot to think about.
Which school is the closest to Riverdale?

courses.title: 第 29 集｜Smell the Flowers｜Act 2
courses.description: 苏珊与哈里和米歇尔共进午餐，米歇尔情绪低落，苏珊试图与她沟通。

sentences.content: Coming up in Act Two, Susan greets Harry and Michelle.
We have both been excited about seeing you and having lunch with you today.
But Michelle may not want to have lunch.
Harry, if Michelle doesn't want to go, we don't have to.
Welcome to the South Street Restaurant.
And Susan tries to talk to Michelle.
Michelle, can we have a talk?
It's nice to see you again.
We have both been excited about seeing you and having lunch with you today.
Michelle picked these flowers out for you.
We're going to go to lunch in a few minutes, honey.
Okay, you go out and get a drink of water at the fountain.
The fountain is over there, Michelle, near the exit sign.
I used to be that way when I was her age.
Harry, if Michelle doesn't want to go, we don't have to.
Remember, I haven't dated anyone else since her mother died.
This is a little difficult for her.
Yes, but could you wait one minute?
I have a call to make.
Sam, get Mr. Levine at Toy Town Stores on the telephone for me, please.
Hello, Susan Stewart calling Mr. Levine, please.
I find myself in an embarrassing situation.
I made another lunch date for today and forgot to enter it in my appointment book.
Can you and I meet for drinks tomorrow?
Welcome to the South Street Restaurant, folks.
Well, the crab salad's always a big hit.
Susan, would you like the crab salad?
Michelle, would you like to try the crab salad, too?
We'll have the three crab salads and a pitcher of lemonade.
Help yourself to, celery and carrots and other vegetables.
We had a summer house on Fire Island.
Sure, you and Mommy used to take me on the ferry boat.
And sometimes at night, we would, go down to the beach and catch crabs, remember?
Yes, with a piece of meat on a string.
I think I'm going to go get us all some vegetables.
Michelle, can I help you with the lemonade?
Michelle, can we have a talk?
I know you miss your mother.
Yes, and I'm not trying to take her place.
Then why are you and Daddy spending so much time together?
Because we like each other, and right now he needs a friend.
And so are you, I think.
I'd like to be your friend, too.
Will you let me be your friend, Michelle?
So, what were you two talking about?
I used to be that way when I was her age.
I used to be that way when I was her age.
We had a summer house on Fire Island.
Sure, you and Mommy used to take me on the ferry boat.
Sure, you and Mommy used to take me on the ferry boat.
And sometimes at night, we would go down to the beach and catch crabs.
You know, Michelle, when I was your age, I used to do a lot of fun things.
I used to play the piano.
Mom would give me lessons on Tuesdays after school.
And I used to play the violin.
I would take lessons every Thursday afternoon.
I used to have long hair like you, Michelle,
Every summer, I would get out my fishing pole and try to catch a big one.
Oh, Harry, you used to be so handsome.
Oh, I used to be so handsome?

courses.title: 第 31 集｜A Place of Our Own｜Act 1
courses.description: 玛丽莲向艾伦咨询买房建议，艾伦分享自己买房经历，鼓励他们拥有自己的家。

sentences.content: In Act One, Marilyn asks Ellen for advice about buying a house.
Richard and I feel that with a baby coming, we need to have our own place to live.
They talk about seeing a real estate agent, someone who sells houses,
and they talk about getting a mortgage, a bank loan, to buy a house.
Maybe we should speak to a real estate agent about a house.
And a bank about a mortgage?
Does Ellen want Richard and Marilyn to buy a house?
Richard and I feel that with a baby coming, we
Need to have our own place to live.
Well, what do you think about Richard and me looking for a small house or an apartment at this point in our lives?
We love having you here, and there is room, and,
And when the baby comes, the baby can stay in your room for a while.
Richard feels we need to find a small house.
I remember when I was pregnant with Richard.
Philip and I were living with Grandma and Grandpa.
Philip was a young doctor, and he kept talking about having a house of our own.
We looked at a lot of houses.
Well, Grandpa wanted to, lend us the money to buy one,
He didn't wanna borrow any money.
When did you buy a house?
I was teaching music, and, Philip was opening his first medical office.
Of course, it was a small house, but just right for us.
Now Richard and I are having a baby, and we probably won't be able to afford a house right away, either.
Why don't you look at some houses, Marilyn?
Look in the real estate section of Sunday's, Times.
Maybe we should speak to a real estate agent about a house.
And a bank about a mortgage.
I'll talk to Richard about it.
I think it's a good idea, Ellen.
We can learn a lot by asking.
And if I can be of any help, let me know.
As a matter of fact, my friend, Virginia Martinelli, is a real estate agent.
You won't believe this, but she sold us our first house and this one.
Well, I'll tell Richard, and we'll go to see her.
Do you think the skirt length is right, Ellen?
Do you think it's too long?
Oh, I think the skirt is just right.
Are you planning to attach a train to it?
No train, just the dress, but I am going to make a headpiece of lace.
And thanks for the advice about the house.
I'll talk to Richard about it the minute he comes home.
And remember, we love having you here.
I remember when I was pregnant with Richard.
Philip and I were living with Grandma and Grandpa.
Philip was a young doctor, and he kept talking about having a house of our own.
I remember when Philip and I wanted a place of our own, like Marilyn and Richard want one now.
All people dream of a place of their own.
Some people dream of a farmhouse in the country.
Other people dream about owning an apartment in the city.
Philip and I had our dreams, too.
Philip wanted a ranch-style house in Riverdale with a front door where his patients could enter his first medical office.
I wanted to live in Riverdale, too,
but I wanted a Spanish-style house like the one I grew up in, with tiles on the roof.
So, we looked in the real estate section of the newspaper.
We read about lots of houses for sale, and we went to see a real estate agent, as Marilyn and Richard are going to do.
We looked at lots and lots of houses, but we didn't have enough money to buy any of them.
Richard and Marilyn don't have much money, either.
Maybe they won't be able to afford a house.
Now Richard and I are having a baby, and we probably won't be able to afford a house right away, either.
We couldn't afford one right away,
and later, after Richard was born,
we bought a house here in Riverdale.
Oh, it was small, and it didn't have much land, but I loved it.
Philip and I both loved it because finally, we had a place of our own.

courses.title: 第 33 集｜A Place of Our Own｜Act 3
courses.description: 玛丽莲和理查德去银行咨询抵押贷款，银行职员莱利询问他们的工作收入，评估还款能力。

sentences.content: In Act Three, Marilyn and Richard go to a bank.
They need a mortgage, a bank loan, to buy a house.
What can I do for you?
We'd like to discuss a mortgage.
The bank officer, Mr. Riley, needs to find out if they can afford to pay back the loan,
so he asks about their jobs.
And Mrs. Stewart, are you working?
Will Marilyn and Richard get a mortgage?
I'm Richard Stewart, and this is my wife, Marilyn.
What can I do for you?
We'd like to discuss a mortgage.
Are you buying a house, or are you refinancing your present home?
We're planning to buy a house.
And we'd like to find out about a mortgage.
We are customers of the bank.
As a matter of fact, my whole family banks here.
I have some questions to ask.
Do you own your house or do you rent?
And Mr. Stewart, what is your occupation?
And Mrs. Stewart, are you working?
Yes, I'm a designer, and I work in a boutique.
Did you bring any savings or salary information, last year's tax forms?
What kind of house did you have in mind?
Well, we're talking about buying a two-bedroom house in Mount Kisco.
Here are the financial details on the house.
Are you prepared to make a 10% down payment?
Do you think we can get a loan?
Do you own any other property, any stocks or bonds?
Then you don't have any collateral.
Perhaps you could get a guarantor, someone to sign for the loan for you.
Since you don't have enough income and you don't already own any property, the bank needs to be sure you can pay the mortgage every month.
A guarantor is responsible for the loan if you can't make the payments.
Well, the idea of buying a house is exciting.
Goodbye, and hope to see you soon.
It all sounded so easy until they mentioned needing collateral or a guarantor.
And I don't think it's a good idea to ask Dad to sign as a guarantor.
I don't feel right about it.
I understand your feelings about it, Richard.
Now tell me, what's the problem?
We can get a loan from the bank if we can put up some collateral.
And we don't own anything to use as collateral.
Or someone can sign with us as a guarantor.
Why don't you speak to Dad?
If we buy a house, I wanna be able to handle it alone.
Oh, everybody needs help sometimes, Richard.
I understand Richard's feelings about it, Ellen.
In two or three months, I'll have an advance on my book and be able to put more money down.
What about the house in Mount Kisco?
Somebody else'll buy it by then.
Well, then there'll be other houses, Marilyn.
We're in no great rush, it's true.
This has been a great learning experience for us, Marilyn, talking to the real estate agent, looking at the houses,
Talking to the loan officer at the bank.
It has been a learning experience, that's true.
I think you're doing the right thing, taking your time, looking around, especially with a purchase of this kind.
You're talking about a lot of money.
We'll call Mrs. Martinelli and tell her to keep looking for us.
And I'll call Mr. Riley at the bank and tell him we'll see him in a couple of months.
And if you ever need Dad or me to help you- We know.
You know we'll be there for you.

And Grandpa tells Mr. Marchetta about his experience in the construction business.
43 years, half that time in my own construction company.

courses.title: 第 39 集｜A Real Stewart｜Act 3
courses.description: 玛丽莲拆开哈里和米歇尔送的婴儿服，苏珊带米歇尔看麦克斯，大家表达对宝宝的爱。

sentences.content: In Act Three, Marilyn opens a gift from Harry and Michelle.
With his name on it, Max.
Susan offers to take Michelle upstairs to see the baby.
Would you like to see Baby Max, Michelle?
What will Michelle think of Max?
With his name on it, Max.
Thanks so much, Harry and Michelle.
Yes, I told Daddy to pick blue ones.
Blue is for boys and pink is for girls.
That was so thoughtful of you, Michelle.
Especially to pick it out in blue.
Would you like to see Baby Max, Michelle?
Harry and Michelle can watch Max sleeping.
Come on, Michelle, before Max wakes up.
Will you please take this upstairs, Susan?
Michelle is very grown up for a 10-year-old, huh?
She's smart and sensitive for her age.
Growing up without a mother is difficult.
Susan's like a mother to Michelle.
Susan and Harry will get married?
Yes, they get along so well.
It's hard to do anything but listen in this family.
How can anybody get a word in around here?
It's the way it should be.
They always were, and they always will be.
And now there's Max Stewart, and if he talks as loudly as he cries, we're all in for trouble.
It's not necessary to whisper, Harry.
A baby gets used to voices.
We always whispered when Michelle was born.
I never slept, and when I did, I woke up when I heard someone speak.
Oh, good, now I can help diaper him.
What do you, what do you do when he cries like that?
A new baby in the Stewart family.
You know what that means, don't you?
That means I, Malcolm Stewart, am now a great-grandfather, and Max is my great-grandson.
My son, Philip, is a grandfather now.
And Ellen's his grandmother, a very loving grandma.
Susan thinks that Max looks like Ellen, but Robbie thinks Max looks like me.
He thinks his little nephew, Max, is pretty special.
Susan, Max's aunt, thinks he's special, too.
And so do his parents, Marilyn and Richard.
Oh, little Max, I love you.
You're a real Stewart, just like me, and just like all of us.

courses.title: 第 41 集｜Playing Games｜Act 2
courses.description: 米歇尔带朋友奥黛丽和库珀太太来玩，苏珊展示公司新游戏，但米歇尔觉得太简单。

sentences.content: In the second act, Michelle arrives with her friends.
I'd like you to meet Audrey and her mother, Mrs. Cooper.
Susan's company has made a new game.
She teaches the girls and Harry how to play it.
The leader takes the first 10 cards and lays them face up on the stand.
But Michelle doesn't really like the game.
Oh, Daddy, I had such a good time at the aquarium.
Michelle, why don't you introduce everybody to Susan?
I'd like you to meet Audrey and her mother, Mrs. Cooper.
Nice to meet you, Mrs. Cooper.
And this is Shirley and Nicole.
I had never been there before.
The girls learned a great deal.
Well, please sit down and tell us all about it during lunch.
We prepared some tuna fish and cheese sandwiches for lunch.
I remember when I used to be a Girl Scout, my mother would take us everywhere too.
Susan, I understand you're in the toy business.
My company manufactures toys and games for children.
Susan's vice president in charge of new toys and games.
And the marketing of new toys and games.
Can we test a new game for you, Susan?
I happen to have a game which I brought home to study.
Don't you want to play, Nicole, Shirley, Audrey?
We tested it last week on 12 to 15-year-olds, and they found it to be too easy.
We think it might be just right for 10 to 12-year-olds.
The leader takes the first 10 cards and lays them face up on the stand.
Everyone gets a turn going counterclockwise, left to right.
30 seconds to make a word using as many letters as possible.
You get one point for each letter, plus the person with the longest word gets 10 extra points.
The first one to get 100 points wins.
Okay, let's go around the table.
Michelle wins with a six-letter word, plus she gets an additional 10 points for a total of 16 points.
How are you enjoying the game so far?
She just said it's too easy.
But we have to get going to meet the rest of the troop at 2:00 at the museum.
Oh, it was nice meeting all of you.
I hope you have a wonderful time at the Museum of Natural History.
See you in front of the museum at 5:00.
And thanks again for the lunch and for the game.
You helped save our company a lot of money.
Isn't there a, conversation that we have to finish?
It's time to play Take My Word.
Here are the rules of the game.
We'll ask you to make some words from these letters.
We'll tell you how many letters are in the word, and we'll give you a clue.
You're looking for a word with three letters.
Max is Susan's nephew, so Susan is Max's what?
You can wear this when it's cold outside.
What do you wear when it's cold outside?
Well, I don't know about you, but I wear a coat.
A three-letter word, and here's your clue.
You can do it with scissors.
Okay, ladies and gentlemen, you can use scissors to cut.
And now a word with five letters.
You can count with your fingers.
And now, friends, for the last word, you must use all 10 letters.
A 10-letter word, and here's your clue.
And that's all the time we have.
Thanks for playing Take My Word.

courses.title: 第 43 集｜Second Honeymoon｜Act 1
courses.description: 理查德送玫瑰庆祝结婚五周年，计划带玛丽莲去水磨坊旅馆度第二次蜜月，但预订出问题。

sentences.content: In Act 1, Richard gives Marilyn a bouquet of roses.
What are the flowers for, Richard?
To celebrate their fifth wedding anniversary, Richard wants to take Marilyn to the Water Mill Inn.
You and I, Mrs. Stewart, are going to spend a second honeymoon at the Water Mill Inn.
What are the flowers for, Richard?
But our anniversary isn't until Saturday.
Besides, we are not going to be here Saturday.
Where are we going to be?
If you had your choice of all the places in the world, where would you choose to spend our anniversary?
I loved that place when we went on our honeymoon.
You and I, Mrs. Stewart, are going to spend a second honeymoon at the Water Mill Inn.
Aren't we taking the baby on our honeymoon?
The world's greatest grandmother, Mrs. Ellen Stewart, has agreed to take care of him for the weekend.
Richard, isn't that too much to ask of your mother?
She loves taking care of Max.
We'll, we'll phone every hour, and you can listen to him over the phone.
Come on, Mar, it's time you and I had a romantic weekend alone together.
I'll make a reservation right now.
Remember that wonderful little balcony where we had our meals, with a view of the Hudson River?
My wife and I spent our honeymoon at the Inn.
No, we didn't leave anything in the room.
We'd like to make a reservation for this weekend.
Can you recommend someplace nice, someplace nearby?
He says there's another inn just a half a mile down the road from the Water Mill.
It won't be the same, but, what do you say?
My mom is available to babysit this weekend.
Hello, is this the Old Country Inn?
The desk clerk at the Water Mill suggested your inn.
Would you happen to have a room for two available this weekend?
My wife and I are celebrating our fifth anniversary.
Yes, we'll be arriving by car about 10:00 Friday night.
You and I, Miss Stewart, are going to have a wonderful, romantic weekend.
I'd like some information about the inn.
We're located in the town of Rhinebeck, just a two-hour drive from the city.
What kinds of accommodations do you have?
For a very special vacation, we have a large honeymoon suite.
Or if you prefer, you can reserve a smaller single room.
Or a double room with a fireplace and a balcony.
And the view of the Hudson River from the balcony is absolutely gorgeous.
Well, the town of Rhinebeck is the perfect place to take an afternoon walk.
And of course, after all that walking,
You'll want to relax and have a delicious dinner in our romantic dining room.
Too tired to come to the dining room?
Our friendly room service is always ready to bring delicious meals to your room.
Our innkeeper, Mrs. Montefiore, is the nicest person you'll ever meet.
She's been making the Water Mill Inn a comfortable place for guests for over 20 years.
Well, you can check in any time after 1:00 PM and check out any time before 12:00 noon.
Now, when would you like your reservations, and what type of room would you like?
You can be sure that the Water Mill Inn is the finest small hotel in all of New York State.

courses.title: 第 45 集｜Second Honeymoon｜Act 3
courses.description: 理查德和玛丽莲入住水磨坊旅馆蜜月套房，与老板交谈，回忆结婚时的美好时光。

sentences.content: In act three, Richard and Marilyn enter the honeymoon suite at the Water Mill Inn.
Welcome to the Water Mill Inn.
Oh, Richard, it's exactly as it was when we were married.
And they enjoy talking with Mrs. Montefiore, the innkeeper.
I remember you and your wife from the first time you stayed with us.
As Mrs. Montefiore leaves the suite, there's a knock at the door.
Welcome to the Water Mill Inn.
Oh, Richard, it's exactly as it was when we were married.
Even the old patchwork quilt is the same.
My great-grandmother made that quilt when Teddy Roosevelt was president.
In those days when they made quilts,
they cut patches from the old clothing of every member in the family,
so that each one would be a part of it.
I remember you and your wife from the first time you stayed with us.
Would a professional photographer be without a picture?
And very good-looking like his mother.
Well, it's nice to have you with us again.
You see, Richard, Max is welcome here.
This vacation is for you and me.
If there's anything you need, please call me.
I'll be in the front office all day.
Oh, I took the liberty of ordering some breakfast for you.
Just put it over there, Charles.
Compliments of the Water Mill Inn.
Now, this is my idea of a good time.
Slices of orange with burnt honey.
First, I wanna call home and check on your mother and the baby.
Honey, if there were any problems, she would call us.
She doesn't know we've changed hotels.
I'd like to call Riverdale, New York.
This food is heavenly, isn't it?
Do you remember that old desk?
Mrs. Montefiore told me that George Washington sat at that desk and wrote to his wife, Martha.
What do you wanna do after breakfast?
Why don't we take a walk down to the river?
Now, this is my idea of a good time.
Looking at our photographs, from all our time together.
I see us both changing through the years.
I can't believe how young we looked.
It seems a million years ago.
But through it all, we've shared our joys and tears.
There we are together, once upon a time.
Reminding me of how we used to be.
There we are together, smiling at the camera.
Each day was bright and new for us.
There we are, the two of us.
And still we are together, you and me.
Every photograph reminds me how I love you.
And how our love gets better every day.
Every photograph reminds me how the years just come and go.
And I can see our love grow
Looking at our photographs, I'm going back in time.
The pictures take me there again.
But we both look so different then.
Could that really be you and me?
Every photograph reminds me how I love you.
And I can see our love grow with every photograph.

courses.title: 第 46 集｜Full of Surprises｜Act 1
courses.description: 爷爷收到大学室友皮特的来信，邀请他参加50周年聚会，爷爷考虑是否前往。

sentences.content: In the first act, a letter arrives for Grandpa.
The return name and address is Pete Waters, RFD Number 1, Chesterton.
Pete Waters is an old friend of Grandpa's.
He was my roommate in college.
In the letter, Pete invites Grandpa to a reunion, a time to see their old friends again.
He's writing to invite me to spend a weekend with him at his farm.
He's planning a get-together with two or three other college friends,
A kind of a 50-year anniversary reunion.
Will Grandpa go to the reunion?
The mailman just dropped some mail in our box, Grandpa.
Oh, probably a lot of advertising and bills.
Why don't you write to me, Robbie, so I can get some interesting mail?
It's just like I said, Robbie,
You won't believe it, Grandpa, but there's a letter here addressed to you, Mr. Malcolm Stewart, and it looks like a personal letter.
The return name and address is Pete Waters, RFD Number 1, Chesterton.
He was my roommate in college.
He visited with, Grandma and me in Florida about five years ago.
He's writing to invite me to spend a weekend with him at his farm.
He's planning a get-together with two or three other college friends,
A kind of a 50-year anniversary reunion.
It sounds like fun to me too, Robbie.
What kind of farm does he have?
I've never been there, Robbie, but he has chickens and cows and all.
That means fresh eggs and fresh milk.
He's not as lucky as I am to have a family and grandchildren.
How come he never got married?
He never married because the girl he was in love with in college married someone else, as simple as that.
He must have loved her very much.
Lillian Winters, she was in our class.
She was in love with Donald McGrath, the quarterback on our football team.
Football players are always popular with the ladies.
She liked Pete, and they went to dances together, but her heart was with Donald.
Did he ever get over it?
Maybe Lillian will be at the reunion.
I wish I could go there with you, Grandpa.
What do you think the surprise will be?
With Pete, you never know, Robbie.
Won't it be exciting to see all your college friends there again?
I'm kind of excited about going now.
Next weekend, sleep over Friday and Saturday night, and come back Sunday.
Don't you think you ought to call Pete and tell him you're coming?
He's planning a get-together with two or three other college friends.
A kind of, fifty year anniversary reunion.
I got a letter in the mail today.
It said, "How you doing, old friend?
I've been thinking about you, so tell me what's new.
I haven't seen you for a long time.
I was thinking about you today.
And if I could, I'd come right over, but you live too far away." The letter said, "Mm,
we're having a celebration." Let's get together,
It's been a while, you gotta show me that smile, and I wanna see you again.
We'll be reunited, and we'll get to know each other again.
I wanna hear those old stories.
I wanna sing an old song.
The letter said, "Bring your camera, take some pictures.
And if you can come, won't you let me know?
You can write or give me a call.
Before you know it, you're gonna feel like the years never passed at all." The letter said, "Mm,
We're having a celebration." Let's get together,
It's been a while, you gotta show me that smile, and I wanna see you again.

courses.title: 第 47 集｜Full of Surprises｜Act 2
courses.description: 爷爷开车去皮特农场，途中向加油站员工和农场工人问路，最终找到目的地。

sentences.content: In the second act, Grandpa is traveling to Pete Water's farm.
the man at the gas station gives him directions for a shortcut, a shorter route to Pete's farm.
You take the next left turn.
Make a right at the stop sign.
Later, a farm worker gives Grandpa more directions.
Keep along this road until you get to the end of the fence.
His house is on the left.
Will Grandpa ever find the farm?
What can I do for you?
Old Pete Water's lived around here almost as long as I have.
How long is it gonna take to, for me to get there?
There's a shortcut, if you know it.
Could you, tell me how to use the shortcut?
You take the next left turn.
Make a right at the stop sign.
Stay on that road and you'll cross a blue bridge.
Then you'll see a big old red barn.
That's the back of Pete Water's place.
Well, that's quite a difference from the directions that Pete sent me.
Now, if you take that route, it's probably a lot simpler, but, take you 10 minutes longer.
Take the next left turn to the stop sign.
Then a right across a blue bridge.
And then a big red barn.
How much do I owe you?
Thank you, and thanks for the directions.
Well, this must be Pete's barn.
What can I do for you?
Is this the Pete Water's farm?
Keep along this road until you get to the end of the fence.
His house is on the left.
Same old Pete Waters, always full of surprises.
Could you, tell me how to use the shortcut?
You take the next left turn.
Make a right at the stop sign.
Stay on that road and you'll cross a blue bridge.
Then you'll see a big old red barn.
You take the next left turn.
Make a right at the stop sign.
Stay on that road and you'll cross a blue bridge.
Then you'll see a big old red barn.
Keep along this road until you get to the end of the fence.
His house is on the left.
Well, I made it to Pete's house, but he's not here.
I think I'd like to see some more of the countryside while I wait for him to get back.
I'll back out of the driveway and be on my way.
Let me back up again and go in the opposite direction and see what I find.
Well, I'd better get back to Pete's.
All I have to do is back out of the driveway,
go to the fork in the road,
then make a right at the first intersection.
Pete's driveway should be the first right turn.

courses.title: 第 48 集｜Full of Surprises｜Act 3
courses.description: 爷爷见到老友佩吉和阿诺德，皮特和莉莉出现，揭示莉莉就是皮特再婚的妻子。

sentences.content: In the third act, Grandpa sees two of his old friends, Peggy Pendleton and Arnold Franklin.
The two of you look unbelievable.
And it's time for the surprise.
Come on, we'll tell you the big surprise.
Except for the beard, he hasn't changed in 50 years.
You haven't changed much in 50 years.
Who am I, you old rascal?
You don't recognize me, do you?
Oh, I know who you are.
Oh, he left a note on the door saying he was going to the, railroad station to pick up a surprise.
The two of you look unbelievable.
Oh, I was sorry to hear about your wife having passed away.
And you're living with your children now, in New York?
Pete wrote us and told us.
Retired and, moved to New York to live with my son and his family.
By the way, what do you think this big surprise is?
It could be most anything, knowing Pete.
Now we'll find out about the surprise.
Pete, oh, it's so good to see you.
We were together in a Thursday night drama society.
Donald passed away a couple years ago.
I would not have missed this get-together for the world.
And you're a little surprised, Pete.
You really surprised me by having us all come together.
You don't know what the surprise is yet?
Come on, we'll tell you the big surprise.
I've invited you here for the weekend to help celebrate.
No, Pete wants to tell you.
Now let me have the honor, Lillian.
For goodness sake, Pete, tell us.
Well, I am pouring this iced tea so that we can toast Lillian and me.
You don't mean to tell me that you Yes, I do.
I have loved Lillian all these years, so I asked her to be Mrs. Pete Waters.
Oh, Lillian, I am so happy for you both.
Lillian will make me a happy man finally.
You are full of surprises, Pete.
We are going to spend the entire weekend having a good time together here on the farm.
We are going to celebrate all weekend.
Lily and I were married two weeks ago in Detroit.
Wait till I tell my family about this.
Pete and Lillian seem so happy.
After all these years, 50 years to be exact.
50 years ago I was a young man.
And Pete was my college roommate, a real pal.
Pete loved Lillian from the moment they met.
Sometimes he'd call the radio station where I was an announcer and ask me to play certain love songs for Lillian.
And he wanted to spend his life with her.
Lil liked Pete, but she fell in love with Donald.
Donald and I were on the Michigan football team.
He was the quarterback and captain.
Was the smallest one on the team.
Then I finally got to play my senior year.
Lil and Donald got married right after college and bought a house in Detroit, Michigan.
Here's a picture of Lil and their son, Donald Jr.
Later, the family grew to include Robert and Barbara.
Meanwhile, Pete stayed single, working hard, conducting orchestras, playing in bands, and teaching music
Until he retired and bought the farm in Chesterton four years ago.
And now Pete and Lil are married and living on his farm.
You never know what's gonna happen.

courses.title: 第 51 集｜Photo Finish｜Act 3
courses.description: 理查德拍摄街头艺人后再次见卡尔森。卡尔森同意出版《走遍美国》，理查德成功完成两周的拍摄任务。

sentences.content: In Act Three, Richard photographs street performers as Mr. Carlson requested.
Later, Richard thinks he's ready to see Mr. Carlson again.
I'm gonna show him the photos on Monday morning.
On Monday, Richard asks Mr. Carlson if he'll publish Family Album USA.
I said I could do it in two weeks, and I did it.
The pictures you've taken are fabulous, Richard.
I'm gonna show him the photos on Monday morning.
You really did a beautiful job.
I know he will love the new photographs for your book.
I really did do a good job, didn't I?
There's still some film left on this roll, and there's one person I haven't photographed in a long time.
And I'm so glad you like them so much.
I'll have a contract and an advance payment waiting for you first thing in the morning.
And while you're here, I would like to introduce you to your editor, and I want you to meet the people in the art department.
I'll set up an appointment with the marketing people.
When do you think we'll be through?
I can't wait to tell Marilyn.
What do you think of that?
What do you think of that?
What do you think of them?
What do you think of him?

courses.title: 第 52 集｜Making a Difference｜Act 1
courses.description: 艾伦发现卡特·博斯韦尔竞选学校董事会并计划削减文化项目。她决定参选以阻止他，菲利普认为博斯韦尔会赢。

sentences.content: In act one, Ellen finds out that Carter Boswell is running for the school board.
He's running for the school board.
Ellen is upset because Boswell wants to cut the school cultural programs.
No music, no dance, no concert, no stage presentations.
Philip thinks Boswell will win the election.
It sounds to me like Carter Boswell is going to win the seat on the board.
Oh, not if I can stop it.
He's running for the school board.
Oh, what's wrong with wanting to be on the school board?
But he wants to cut the school budget.
Cutting the budget is fine, but he wants to do it by cutting all the cultural programs.
No music, no dance, no concert, no stage presentations.
Why does he want to do that?
He says it's to save the taxpayers money,
and I think he believes that the taxpayers will vote for him if he spends less on the cultural programs.
Lots of people want their taxes used for new books and a new paint job in the school rooms.
Maybe some of us would like to pay a little bit more and keep the cultural programs for our kids.
I hear it from my patients.
Lots of people are tired of higher taxes.
But if Boswell wins, he'll be an important decision-maker on the school board, and he doesn't know anything about our children's education.
Well, it sounds to me like Carter Boswell is going to win the seat on the board.
Oh, not if I can stop him.
And, how are you going to stop him?
Why shouldn't you run for what, Mom?
Your mother is thinking of running for the school board.
Well, if I run for office, the voters will have a clear choice.
I stand for everything Boswell doesn't.
I think a lot of people will vote for you against Boswell, Ellen.
Will you help me if I do run?
The trouble is it takes a little bit of money to run a campaign.
I think you can make a difference, Ellen, and in a short campaign, you wouldn't need as much money.
Why not give the people of Riverdale a clear choice?
What would you like to see me about?
Well, I'm editor of the most influential newspaper in Riverdale.
A lot of people would like my help.
I'm planning to run for the school board.
Will you announce that I'm running?
Why will the voters vote for you against Boswell, Mrs. Stewart?
"Vote for Ellen Stewart, she cares." Not a bad slogan.
But, what do you care about?
Well, I care about the children of our town.
I don't want them to grow up without cultural programs in our school.
I want our children to learn more than reading, writing, and arithmetic.
I want to keep the after-school programs, the music, the concerts
But who's gonna pay for all of this?
The citizens of Riverdale, of course.
I plan to get help from the businessmen and the corporations of Riverdale.
Exactly what do you want from me, Mrs. Stewart?
I can't expect you to take my side against Boswell.
But I do need some publicity so that the people of our town know that I'm running for office and that I care about our children
I certainly can print the news, and you are now making news
Why will the voters vote for you against Boswell, Mrs. Stewart?
She cares." Not a bad slogan
It is a good campaign slogan.
People will hear it and know what I stand for.
I care about our children's education,
Not just the school buildings themselves, but the children.
I care about what children study and what they learn.
I want them to learn about a variety of subjects, including music and literature and art.
And I care about our children's activities after school.
I want to keep their music programs, like the orchestra.
I want children to experience the joys of music.
I play the piano myself, and I've taught music to many children in Riverdale.
I want to keep the other after-school programs, too.
I'll get local businesses, banks, and other companies in the community to help.
We all have children in this town,
and I believe that parents care about education,
and I want to be on the Riverdale School Board.
I know it's a big responsibility, but I know I can make a difference,

courses.title: 第 53 集｜Making a Difference｜Act 2
courses.description: 全家帮助艾伦竞选：爷爷印传单，玛丽莲和理查德准备信封，罗比宣传。电视上博斯韦尔的广告引发担忧。

sentences.content: In Act Two, everyone helps Ellen and her campaign.
Here are the flyers, hot off the press.
Marilyn and Richard prepare the envelopes.
And Robbie and his friends tell people about Ellen's campaign.
Did you know my mother is running for the school board?
Later, the family sees Boswell in a commercial on television.
And if you ask what I care about, I'll tell you.
Here are the flyers, hot off the press.
Richard and I will put them into the envelopes.
Can I speak with Mr. and Mrs. Anderson?
Did you know my mother is running for the school board?
I'll see you at the polls.
I'll give her your best wishes, Mr. Nelson.
Can I speak with Mr. and Mrs. Burns?
We have done so much in such a short amount of time, I can't believe it.
Wait till Philip comes home and sees our progress.
Everyone saw the story in the Riverdale newspaper.
Mr. Maxwell was very kind to print my announcement.
Everybody in Riverdale reads his paper.
Your photo in it helped, too.
Hey, everybody, Mrs. Greenberg is on the phone.
She says Carter Boswell is on the TV right now doing a commercial.
And if you ask what I care about, I'll tell you.
I care about the school buildings in need of paint.
I care about more lockers for the teachers.
I care about new fixtures in the hallways.
Not music or dancing or entertainment.
I care about the practical things.
If you do, vote for me, Carter Boswell.
A lot of people will agree with him.
It's our school, but we can't vote.
There are people in favor of the cultural programs, Mom.
Don't be upset by Boswell's commercial.
You have to go on television, too.
Get out and vote on election day.
We need your vote if you want better schools.
Ellen Stewart's running for the school board.
And we know she can't be beat.
Ellen Stewart's running for the school board.
And we know she can't be beat.
And if you want your vote to count, Ellen Stewart is the one to choose.
Come on, let's fight for Ellen Stewart.
That Ellen Stewart is the one who cares.
She'll make a difference for everyone.
She knows the importance of music and art.
Cultural programs play a big part.
Let's keep these programs in our schools.
Ellen Stewart's for me and you.
So let's all give her a cheer.

courses.title: 第 54 集｜Making a Difference｜Act 3
courses.description: 理查德和罗比录制艾伦的竞选演讲并播放。选举中艾伦领先，最终获胜并被任命为文化项目委员会成员。

sentences.content: In act three, Richard and Robbie make a videotape of Ellen as she gives her campaign speech
And Richard figures out a way for people to see the videotape.
Later, the family listens to the election news.
In the hotly contested race for the one seat on the Riverdale School Board, Mrs. Ellen Stewart has taken an early lead.
I care about people, not things.
My name is Ellen Stewart, and I'm running for the open seat on the school board.
What does the word care mean?
I care about people, not things.
How can we possibly get it on so Riverdale will see it and hear it?
I mean that when I say I care.
I care about people, not things.
Mom is now on television, in every appliance store in Riverdale, except Hamlin's.
We got our brains from you, Dad.
Their TV news is gonna cover it.
"Housewife campaigns in appliance stores." And I'll bet some magazine will pick up the story, too.
I know we're getting some attention now, but
In the end, the voters will have to decide.
In the hotly contested race for the one seat on the Riverdale School Board, Mrs. Ellen Stewart has taken an early lead.
Now turning to other local news.
Riverdale High School- Well, it's too soon to know for certain.
The tallest man in baseball- Well, you're ahead.
Boss of the Texas- It's not over yet.
Let's, let's just all calm down and wait for the final results.
Why don't you go out to the backyard and get some fresh air?
You lost by a very small number of votes.
Look, you made a very strong impression on our community.
You'll have another chance next election.
I just called to tell you that you were very impressive.
You lost the election, but you won the attention of the residents of Riverdale, of Boswell, and of me.
Well, th- thank you, Mr. Maxwell.
I hear Boswell wants to appoint you to a special arts committee.
I'm sending over a reporter in the morning to interview you.
I'm gonna do an article on Ellen Stewart: She Cares.
I did make a difference in town.
An important local election took place today in Riverdale.
The people of this community elected a new member of the school board, Carter Boswell.
Opposing him in the campaign was Ellen Stewart, a housewife from Riverdale.
Tonight, we'll take a look at both campaigns.
First, we turn to the Boswell campaign.
Mr. Boswell reached many voters by appearing on local TV.
I care about the school buildings in need of paint.
I care about more lockers for the teachers.
I care about new fixtures in the hallways.
Less than a month ago, a new face entered the race: Ellen Stewart.
Mrs. Stewart disagreed with Carter Boswell's plans for the Riverdale schools.
She campaigned very strongly to keep the cultural programs in music, art, and drama.
Local appliance stores played a videotape of Mrs. Stewart introducing herself to the voters.
My name is Ellen Stewart, and I'm running for the open seat on the school board.
My slogan is, "I care." I care about people, not things.
Mrs. Stewart's unusual campaign helped her win the attention of the local newspaper.
Charles Maxwell, the editor of the Riverdale News, praised Mrs. Stewart for caring about the cultural programs in the schools.
When the first votes were counted early in the day,
it seemed as if Ellen Stewart might win a surprise victory over Carter Boswell,
but once all the votes were counted, Mrs. Stewart lost by only one hundred twenty-one votes.
Well, it was a very close election, and Ellen Stewart convinced the people of Riverdale that she cared.
who now wants to appoint Mrs. Stewart to a special committee for cultural programs in the schools.
Well, that's our special election day report on a very important local election.
Thank you, and have a good evening.

courses.title: 第 55 集｜I Do｜Act 1
courses.description: 苏珊和哈里婚礼当天，哈里紧张不安，菲利普和爷爷帮忙。哈里担心弄丢戒指，最终找到。

sentences.content: Today, Susan Stewart and Harry Bennett are getting married.
Coming up in Act One, Harry gets ready.
Philip tries to help Harry with his bow tie.
What if we can't tie the tie?
Harry is very nervous, and Grandpa tries to calm him down.
Later, Harry worries that he's lost something important.
What did I do with the rings?
What did I do with the rings?
Will Harry find the wedding rings?
Are they always that difficult to make?
At this rate, the wedding will take place tomorrow.
What if we can't tie the tie?
If we can't tie the tie, then there can't be a wedding.
You better not make Harry any more nervous than he is.
Don't worry, we'll figure a way.
We can't get this bow tie tied.
Nobody knows how to do it.
Well, you have your own tuxedo.
How do you tie your bow tie?
Yeah, Grandpa, I've seen you in it.
I never could tie one of those things, bow ties.
I have always worn a clip-on bow tie.
All you do is clip it around under your collar.
We all need one of those.
The tuxedo rental store, do you think they're open?
Well, if they're not, I'll lend you mine, Harry.
You're the only one who really needs to be wearing a tuxedo anyway.
I'm the father of the bride.
I'm supposed to be worried about my daughter, and here I am with the man that's marrying my daughter, worrying about him.
They're open, and they have lots of clip-on bow ties.
I'll bicycle down to the village and get them.
In two hours and 15 minutes, I'll be married to Susan.
And be a true member of the Stewart family.
Oh, you're a lucky guy, Harry.
Susan is one of the best women you'll ever find.
Now, once you put the ring on Susan's finger, you are one of us, Harry.
What did I do with the rings?
I put them in the pocket of my sports jacket.
No, I think you put them in your tuxedo jacket pocket.
What did I do with the rings?
Didn't you give them to Richard?
What did I do with them?
Oh, don't worry, Harry, they have to be here.
I gave them to Robbie to hold so I wouldn't lose them.
Robbie went to pick up the clip-on bow ties.
There's still a little over two hours, Harry.
He gave them to me to hold onto them, because he didn't want the responsibility of holding them.
I put them in my tuxedo, but
I'll hold onto them for you.
The best man always keeps the rings.
You hold onto them, so there won't be a problem later.
Well, I think we'd better get dressed, fellas.
Robbie will bring the ties back.
It'll all be over in two hours.
The wedding ceremony will be over.
Oh, that's a long time to wait.
I do have the wedding day jitters.
I couldn't find the rings, but they were in my pocket.
I don't need to worry about that.
None of us knew how to tie my bow tie, but that problem's taken care of now, too,
Since Robbie went into the village to pick up some clip-on bow ties.
I'll be married to the most wonderful woman in the world,
I fell in love with Susan on, our very first date.
I think we're gonna be good friends.
She'll be a wonderful mother to Michelle.
And soon she'll be my wife,
But I couldn't be any happier.

courses.description: 斯图尔特一家和朋友们聚集在庭院，法官主持婚礼；交换戒指时，哈里让大家小小紧张了一下。

sentences.content: In the final act, the Stewart family and friends gather for the wedding, and the judge begins.

courses.title: 第 59 集｜Quality Time｜Act 2
courses.description: 罗比向艾伦表达感受，认为父母工作太忙。他建议父母单独度假，但艾伦觉得太忙。罗比提出一个主意，让父母一起参与阅读项目。

sentences.content: In Act Two, Robbie tells Ellen how he feels.
Dad works hard, and he works late.
You work hard on all your committees, and you work late.
Robbie wants his parents to spend some time together.
I think you ought to take a vacation away from the family, alone.
But Ellen knows that she and Philip are too busy to take a vacation, so Robbie tries again.
I think I have an idea.
What are you doing up this late?
Come on, Robbie, what are you doing up this late?
Do you care to talk about them?
Sure, if you don't mind listening.
If you have something you wanna talk about, I'm always prepared to listen.
You haven't been around much lately.
You and Dad are like ships that pass in the night.
Dad works hard, and he works late.
You work hard on all your committees, and you work late.
I thought you were proud of the work I do.
I've been noticing how little quality time you spend with Dad and me, and the family.
There must be a way that Dad and you can spend more time together.
Well, we always talk about taking a vacation together, with the family.
I think you ought to take a vacation away from the family, alone.
It would be wonderful, but our schedules won't allow it.
I think I have an idea.
I think I have an idea that will bring Dad and you together in a more scheduled way.
Well, you know how Dad is always talking about the kids in the ward, and how important it is for them to be paid attention to?
Well, and how hard it is because the doctors and nurses are so busy?
Well, how would it be if you took some time to work with Dad towards solving that problem?
Like setting up a regular weekly reading program.
You and Dr. Philip Stewart going to the children's ward once or twice a week and reading to them.
As a matter of fact, it fits right in with something I'm working on right now with the school board committee.
I've been trying to work out a program in the public school.
It will bring parents and teachers together once a week to read to the students, their own children, really.
By doing that, it will encourage reading.
So it might fit in with a program for reading to the kids in the hospital.
I'm gonna talk to Daddy about it right now.
But Dad was so exhausted when he came home from work.
Why don't you talk to him about it tomorrow?
You are a very smart young man, Robbie.
I think I'll wait until tomorrow.
It is a great idea, and I promise you I won't forget.
Run that by me again, 'cause I don't understand.
Explain it all again 'cause I don't understand.
What are you trying to say?
What are you trying to say?
Run that by me again, 'cause I don't understand.
Oh, I see what you mean.
Yeah, I see what you're trying to say.
Oh, I know what you mean.

courses.description: 艾伦告诉菲利普她的阅读项目计划，让全家参与。菲利普认为在医院也适用，两人决定合作。他们讨论给孩子们读什么书。

sentences.content: In act three, Ellen tells Philip about her project.
The plan is a simple one: involve the entire family in a reading project.
Philip thinks the project would work in hospitals.
My patients, mostly kids, would love to read and be read to.
So Ellen and Philip agree to work together.
Would you work with me on it?
Oh, I would love to, Philip.
What will Ellen and Philip read to the children?
That's why I'm reading my paper and having my coffee on the patio this morning.
How was your school board meeting last night?
You must have come home very late.
Well, did you find the sandwich I made for you?
I was so tired I didn't even finish it.
I've been working on a special project with the school board, and I'd like your opinion about it.
I've been trying to find a way to encourage reading.
Well, I think I may have found a way to do it.
I work with families every day, Ellen.
I see how people spend their leisure time, young and old.
Well, that would be okay if, and I repeat, if
People took the time to read.
I couldn't agree with you more.
The question is, how do we get them to read more?
I think you're gonna give me the answer to that question.
You have that look in your eye.
I do have an answer, Philip, or at least I think I do.
The plan is a simple one: involve the entire family in a reading project.
Yes, in the home, but first in the schoolrooms.
But how do you plan to do that?
By arranging with the public schools to schedule one hour a week to start with.
During that time, parents are invited to attend and to read along with the children, their children.
It can go beyond the school system, Ellen.
I guarantee you it would go very well in the hospitals.
Yes, my patients, mostly kids, would love to read and be read to.
Maybe we can experiment with your patients and see how the plan works.
Would you work with me on it?
And, that way, we will spend more time together, Ellen.
We just don't see each other anymore.
You and I are very busy these days.
We need to find time to be together more, to do things together more, you and I.
This would be a wonderful way to accomplish that.
To the patients in the ward?
Well, let's you and I talk about it.
What would you like to read to them?
Mrs. Stewart and I will read a poem by Robert Frost.
It's called Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening.
Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
"Whose woods these are I think I know.
His house is in the village though.
He will not see me stopping here to watch his woods fill up with snow.
My little horse must think it queer to stop without a farmhouse near, between the woods and frozen lake,
The darkest evening of the year.
He gives his harness bells a shake to ask if there's some mistake.
The only other sounds, the sweep of easy wind and downy flake.
The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
but I have promises to keep and miles to go before I sleep.

We've been listening to you both.
Well, we may read together aloud at home.

courses.description: 苏珊告诉爷爷哈里得到洛杉矶的工作机会。她担心搬家对米歇尔的影响以及自己能否找到好工作。哈里了解更多工作细节，犹豫是否接受。

courses.title: 第 63 集｜A Big Fish in a Little Pond｜Act 3
courses.description: 苏珊和米歇尔讨论搬家感受。米歇尔喜欢学校和朋友。哈里回家后，苏珊表达顾虑。哈里做出决定，他选择留在纽约，做小池塘里的大鱼。

sentences.content: In Act Three, Susan and Michelle talk about moving to Los Angeles.
How do you feel about it?
Later, when Harry gets home, Susan explains how she and Michelle feel.
Michelle and I have all kinds of feelings about leaving New York, the family and friends.
Harry listens to them, but it's time for him to make a decision.
Now, tell us about your talk with Mr. York.
Do you think Harry took the job?
I have so many good friends there now.
I wouldn't miss a day even if I were really sick.
Come and sit down for a minute, Michelle.
I'd like to talk to you about something important.
But your daddy and I are talking about something that I'd like your opinion about.
I heard you talking about it the other night when I was trying on my new clothes.
It's about moving to Los Angeles.
How do you feel about it?
Well, I really wouldn't want to move, but- But?
But if you and Daddy want to do, I guess you know what's best for the family and for me.
That's very considerate of you, Michelle.
I'd miss them a lot, but I know what it feels like to miss someone.
We don't have to move if you're not going to be happy about it.
He's going to tell us tonight about the job offer.
Michelle was chosen to do the school poster for the play this year.
And how was your day, Susan?
I see you're in a good mood.
Why don't you tell us about your day?
It's okay to talk about it, Harry.
Michelle and I have all kinds of feelings about leaving New York, the family and friends.
But if you think you should take the job, we're behind you.
We'll move after the school term.
I'll make new friends wherever we are, as long as we're together.
Whatever you think is right for you is right for us.
The two of you are really something.
Now, tell us about your talk with Mr. York.
No, I did not take the job.
But Daddy, I thought- Harry, you didn't turn it down because of me.
No, I turned it down because of me.
Well, I began to think about you and about Michelle,
And then I asked myself, "Do I really wanna work for the biggest company in the country?"
I went into business for myself because I like being my own boss.
I'm a big fish in a little pond.
And I'm not really sure I wanna be a little fish in a big pond.
Oh, Daddy, does that mean we don't have to move?
I couldn't be more sure, Susan.
I'm glad if you are, Harry.
And besides, how could I live in Los Angeles when all my favorite people live here?
I kept asking myself, "Do I really wanna work for the biggest company in the country?"
The company is Crafton Craft, the biggest accounting company in the country.
And they're big, all right, with offices all over the country.
All together, they have 86 offices in the US alone, and one of those offices is in Los Angeles, and that's where I'd be.
Harry Bennett, just one accountant in a huge company full of accountants.
I'd be one little fish in a big pond full of accountants.
Do you wanna be a little fish
And I'm not really sure I wanna be a little fish in a big pond.
I like being my own boss.
I work hard, but I make my own schedule.
I can take time off when I want to, and I choose my own clients.
I have a client in the garment business on 7th Avenue.
I do his taxes every year.
He and my other clients know me personally, and I know them.
They tell me I make a big difference in their businesses, and I do it my way, as president of my own company.
I guess you could say I like being a big fish in my own little pond.
He wants to be a big fish in a little pond, a little pond.

courses.title: 第 66 集｜Career Choices｜Act 3
courses.description: 玛丽莲告诉丽塔·梅决定做全职妈妈，丽塔·梅虽失望但尊重。随后玛丽莲透露计划在家设计婚纱，丽塔·梅对此想法感到好奇。

sentences.content: In the third act, Marilyn tells Rita May about her decision to stay at home with Max.
I've decided to stay at home and be a full-time mother.
Rita May isn't happy with the decision, of course.
I'm disappointed, but I respect your decision.
But then, Marilyn tells Rita May about her plans to design wedding dresses at home.
What kind of dresses would you design?
I've thought about that for some time.
What will she think of the idea?
Whoa, she sure got here quickly.
She must like you and your work, Marilyn.
I think she's just anxious to see Max.
So nice of you to come.
Oh, I just wanted to see your baby Max.
Oh, I met you from the hospital.
It's just a little present for Max.
Can I get you some coffee or tea or a cold drink, Rita May?
Well, I will leave you two to talk.
Let me know if you need anything.
You sounded like you made a decision when you called me.
I have made a decision, Rita May.
I've decided to stay at home and be a full-time mother.
Oh, I'm disappointed, but I respect your decision.
If I had a child as cute as Max, I might do the same thing.
But I haven't finished telling you the other half of my decision.
I think I can stay at home and take care of Max and continue my career.
Do you remember our talks about custom-designed dresses for the boutique?
Why can't I design dresses for you here at home, and make them here, have the fittings here, too?
And I could do the selling and the pricing at the boutique.
What kind of dresses would you design?
I've thought about that for some time.
There's a big market today in wedding dresses.
I like the idea very much.
And if it's successful, we can expand to all kinds of dresses.
As a matter of fact, I have a customer for your first wedding dress.
Well, my niece is getting married, and I've been trying to find just the right thing for her.
Marilyn, you're going to design my niece's dress.
That'll be our first one, and then we'll use it to sell others.
Well, it's a simple idea, and it will work.
Oh, you can certainly design dresses, I know that, and there's no reason why you can't do it from your home.
I can't wait to tell Richard.
Oh, if I had a baby like Max, I'd wanna stay home and be near him all the time, too.
You're making the right decision for Max, and for yourself, too, Marilyn.
Well, now the hard work begins.
Would you like to see some of my designs that I've been working on?
You can certainly design dresses, I know that, and there's no reason why you can't do it from your home.
I can design wedding dresses and continue my career, and I can take care of Max right here at home.
She can do it right here at home.
I wanna stay at home while Max is still a baby.
If I went back to work at the boutique now, Max would be on my mind all the time.
She would only think about Max.
But the truth is, I need to work.
Richard and I want to buy a house, but we can't afford it.
Like most families, we need two incomes in order to afford a house someday.
With a yard and trees and a swing for Max.
More and more families have working mothers.
In the US, more than half of all mothers with preschool children are working at a career.
They have to work and be a mother, too.
And about three-fourths of all mothers with school-aged children are working.
In lots of families, relatives like grandparents offer to take care of children while the parents are working,
and some families bring their children to daycare centers, where other people take care of them.
They stay at daycare centers while their mothers work.
But for now, Max will stay here, and I'll take care of him.
Marilyn and Max will both be at home.
Marilyn will work, and Max won't be alone.

courses.description: 罗比和亚历山德拉迟到，但带来了《河谷报》编辑查尔斯·麦克斯韦。麦克斯韦听取计划后，提出需要召集各代志愿者来推动项目。

sentences.content: In Act Three, Robbie and Alexandra finally arrive.

Men and women, young and old, to give us their time.

Oh, here, on the ground floor, we have the reception area.
Charles Maxwell lived up to his word.

You could call it a community unity plan.
and it needs your contributions of furniture, paint, brushes, ladders, lamps, et cetera.
