courses.description: 罗比邀请亚历山德拉参加周六派对，但未告知是惊喜。派对准备时，亚历山德拉来电，声音沮丧，似乎有事发生。

sentences.content: In act two, Robbie invites Alexandra to the party.
Would you be able to come over Saturday night?
But he doesn't tell her that the party is for her.
My folks are giving me a little graduation party.
On Saturday, Robbie and his friends get ready for Alexandra's surprise party.
Robbie, there's a phone call for you.
You ready for the next problem?
I can't look at another number.
Oh, by the way, when is your plane reservation for your flight to Athens?
Would you be able to come over Saturday night?
I should be finished packing by then.
My folks are giving me a little graduation party.
My dad's letting me borrow the car.
Oh, well, that would be very nice.
Just my friend, Mike, and a few kids from school.
I'm gonna miss all of you.
You've been like a second family to me.
Maybe you could come to visit me in Greece.
Are you excited about graduating from high school?
I was when I first came to the United States.
I'd never been away from home, and I didn't know what it would be like.
But then I found out that people are the same everywhere, once you get to know them.
I'm glad I got to know you.
I'm glad I got to know you,
Wouldn't it be nice if we could skip the examinations and get right to the graduation party?
It would be very nice, but that isn't the way it works.
The Molinas are waiting for me.
I'll pick you up on Saturday night, okay?
She's really a good friend, isn't she?
You are going to miss her.
Am I going to miss her?
You are going to miss her.
And my math teacher's going to miss her.
Well, you can write to her.
You're sure Alexandra's gonna be surprised?
She has no idea that the party is in her honor.
Millie, did you bring the tapes for dancing?
I can't wait to see her face when she walks in here tonight.
My mom's decorating it right now.
Robbie, there's a phone call for you.
Wouldn't it be nice if we could skip the examinations and get right to the graduation party?
There will be no exams this year.
If they really cancel the exams, Robbie would give his big graduation party today,
and if the big party was today- Ha ha.
I mean, if the big party were today,
he would tell all his friends about it,
and if all his friends came to the big party, Robbie would shop for lots of food.
He would buy all the food for the big party if he went shopping in the supermarket.
Ice cream, soda, candy, and cake.
Whoo Everyone would have a great time at Robbie's big party if he bought all that food.
Hey, Robbie, you sure know how to throw a party.
If Robbie played some more music, everyone could be dancing and having fun at the big party.
And if the big party wasn't much fun- Ha ha.
If the big party weren't much fun anymore, everyone might go home.
And if everyone left the big party, Robbie would be alone.
It would be great if the exams were really canceled.
But they're not, so study, Robbie, study.

courses.title: 第 72 集｜Parting Friends｜Act 3
courses.description: 亚历山德拉因航班取消需提前离开，无法参加派对。朋友们担心罗比失望，考虑撤掉装饰。罗比从机场回来，神情低落，不知能否再见。

sentences.content: In Act Three, Robbie's friends are disappointed because Alexandra can't come to the party.
Did she say why she had to leave today?
She told Robbie that her flight tomorrow was canceled, so she had to take an earlier flight today.
They're afraid that Robbie will be disappointed, too.
Do you think we should take down the decorations?
We should have done it sooner.
When Robbie returns from the airport, he does seem upset.
Will Robbie ever see Alexandra again?
No, let's wait till Robbie gets back from the airport.
Did she say why she had to leave today?
She told Robbie that her flight tomorrow was canceled, so she had to take an earlier flight today.
Why is he blowing his horn like that?
Do you think we should take down the decorations?
We should have done it sooner.
Okay, I guess, especially when Alexandra gave me a surprise.
I called my parents from the airport.
When I told them my friends were giving me a party, they insisted that I stay, so now I'm taking a flight on Monday instead.
But how did you know the party was for you?
Well, Robbie told me when he gave me this.
All right, now we can really start the party.
I'd like to say something first.
I would just like to thank all of you, my friends,
Who have made my stay in the United States so wonderful,
and to Robbie and the Stewart family for opening their home to me.
And I also have a little surprise for you, Robbie,
I think you might be amused.
I guess we were thinking the same thought.
"In friendship always, Alexandra." I knew we thought alike, but this is too much.
All right, let's have some music.
I imagine he'The Stewart makes a wonderful wine.
Mrs. Stewart, may I have this dance?
You've become my friend, though I haven't known you very long.
You've always made me feel so right at home.
I can always be myself with you, and when I think of you, I'm not alone.
You were always there when I needed you, never had to ask for anything.
You were there to help me through.
I remember all the times that we spent together having fun.
I won't forget a moment that we shared.
I won't forget your smile, won't forget the way you made me laugh,
the things you did to show me that you cared.
It's hard to say goodbye 'cause you're my friend.
But sometime in the future, we don't know where or when.

courses.title: 第 74 集｜Country Music｜Act 2
courses.description: 玛丽莲、理查德、哈里和苏珊到达露营地，哈里指导搭帐篷生火，玛丽莲受乡村声音启发。

sentences.content: In Act Two, Marilyn, Richard, Harry, and Susan arrive at their campsite.
Harry has been camping before, and he knows what to do.
Well, we'll put everything over there.
We'll set up our tents over there by the edge of the woods, then we'll be able to make our fire there where it's safe.
Later, Marilyn and Richard listen to the sounds of the country.
I've been having a hard time keeping my eyes open just listening to it.
To be away from the city on such a beautiful day is my idea of heaven.
I told you you'd like it.
I've been doing this for years.
You have the spirit of a teenager, Susan.
Wait till you see yourself jumping around.
That's what I love about Susan.
She works hard, she plays hard.
Come on, Richard, help me get this stuff out of the car.
Well, we'll put everything over there.
We'll set up our tents over there by the edge of the woods, then we'll be able to make our fire there where it's safe.
Oh, and there's our table and benches, all set for eating.
That's what makes this spot so good.
When you're out in the fresh air like this, it makes you hungry.
You guys are like three kids.
Well, yeah, now that you mention it, I guess I am.
I mean, how could a guy not be hungry with all this talk about eating?
Where's the bag with the chicken salad sandwiches?
Right here, next to the ice packs.
Here, put the tablecloth on the picnic table, and I will bring the cola and the plastic cups.

courses.title: 第 76 集｜Opening Night｜Act 1
courses.description: 理查德的出版商筹备摄影展，他紧张不安，一位重要评论员前来参观作品。

sentences.content: In Act 1, Richard's publisher is preparing an exhibit, a show with Richard's photographs.
The next thing they'll see is this enlargement with the words Family Album USA.
Later, a newspaper critic arrives to review Richard's work.
Mitchell, so nice of you to come.
Mitchell is one of the most important syndicated reviewers in the country.
A little further to the right, Tom.
It's the first thing people will see when they come in.
It sets the tone for the whole show.
The next thing they'll see is this enlargement with the words Family Album USA.
I can't believe this is really happening.
Years of work went into these pictures.
I know, but it's still a dream come true.
we're not sure what the critics are going to write about your show yet,
and you never know what the man from The New York Times is going to say about it.
The reviews of this show are important for the sales of your book.
Well, when do we see the reviews?
One of the critics is coming over this morning for a preview.
I hope he's in a good mood.
Marilyn and I hope to use money from the sales of this book to buy a new house.
The book will be a success, and the show will help promote it.
Do I really have to autograph copies for the guests at the opening?
A lot of people come to openings just so they can get the autograph of somebody who may be famous someday.
Couldn't we wait until I'm famous?
That might be sooner than you think.
This one over here, Mr. Carlson?
It's too close to the refreshments.
No, I think this one belongs in the people at work section.
How many people will you be bringing?
My wife, Marilyn, my father and mother, my brother, Robbie, my sister and her husband and their daughter, and my grandfather.
No such thing as too many at an opening.
They stood by me through all this.
Mitchell, so nice of you to come.
Mitchell is one of the most important syndicated reviewers in the country.
Well, you're the young man who did all this.
Nice to meet you, Mr. Johnson.

Well, do you mind if I look around and see what it says to me?
What does that mean when he goes, "Mm-hmm.
It probably means he's clearing his throat.
I don't care what the critics say, Mr. Stewart, your work is brilliant.
Tom is studying photography at NYU.
He's working with me during the summer months as an intern.
I'd like to see your work.
It's not good enough to show.
Well, I'd still like to see your work.
You may be the next Ansel Adams and not even know it.
If you really mean it, I'll bring some of my pictures into the gallery.
You have a most unusual eye.
Are you going to be reviewing the show, Mitchell?
Oh, you know I never answer that question, Harvey.
I'd like an advance copy of the book, though, so I can study it.
I have an autographed one in my office.
Would you get Mr. Johnson the copy of Richard's book on my desk?
Do you think he liked my photographs?
We'll know when tonight's papers come out.
This is a job for Pronunciation Man.
If you can hear the difference.
When he said hmm, he meant he was thinking.
Now would you like to take a look at a few paintings?
Note the interesting use of line.
Can you see the forced perspective in this painting?
This is a portrait of the artist's mother.
This is one of my favorites.
Notice the use of black and blue.

sentences.content: In Act Three, Mr. Carlson gives Richard a newspaper.
But Richard is too nervous to read it.

"Richard Stewart's show at the Carlson Gallery is a collection of photographs from his new book, entitled Family Album USA."
Later, Mr. Carlson introduces Richard and Marilyn to John O'Neill.
Richard, Marilyn, I want you to meet John O'Neill.
Mr. O'Neill is a magazine publisher, and he offers Richard a job.
"Richard Stewart's show at the Carlson Gallery is a collection of photographs from his new book, entitled Family Album USA.
There is power and beauty in Mr. Stewart's work, and his book introduces us to a remarkable new talent." Oh, Richard, it's wonderful.
Ladies and gentlemen, if I may have your attention for a moment, please.
I hope you're all enjoying the exhibition.
And I would like to introduce the young man who spent the last five years taking these remarkable pictures.
He also wrote the background for Family Album USA, Mr. Richard Stewart.
I want to thank all of you for coming here tonight.
I'd like to thank Harvey Carlson for his faith in my project,
I would like to thank my family for their love and support all through this adventure.
Hope it wins a Pulitzer Prize.
I'll set up her name in my photography course.

I've been looking forward to meeting your husband, Mrs. Stewart.
I'm really impressed by your show.
In fact, I'd like your autograph.
Mr. O'Neill is the publisher of several magazine.
Oh, of course, I've seen you on television.
Mr. O'Neill was so impressed with your work that he wants to develop it into a magazine concept.
Well, that sounds very exciting, but where would I fit into the plan?
I'd like you to be the photo editor of the magazine.
The problem is that I'm a photographer, not an editor.
In fact, I love what I do, which is going out with a camera and a roll of film and seeing the wonder of humanity.
Now, I appreciate your offer, but I've worked so hard on Family Album USA, and I'm giving some thought to a new book on a different subject.
I'm flattered, but I enjoy taking pictures, and I wanna continue doing that.
Thank you, but I'm happy being a photographer.
Richard, I know your next book will be a success.
I can see our love grow.
There's a lot of love here.
and I'll try to make you happy every day.
